title: A required note is enforced on submit and listed in outstanding items
preconditions:
1. A template has a checkbox field with 'Note required if Monitor / Not OK' on.
2. You are filling an inspection (Work Order Lines — Create & Edit.)
steps:
1. Mark the field Monitor or Not OK and leave the note empty.
2. Try to submit.
3. Check the outstanding-items list before submit.
expected:
1. When the option is on and the response is Monitor or Not OK, a note is required before the inspection can be submitted.
2. The requirement is enforced on submit, not only while filling.
3. Before submit, the field appears in the outstanding-items list so the technician is not rejected by an avoidable error.
4. On a per-axle field the requirement triggers when any axle is marked Monitor or Not OK.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9099 (S1, Require a note on flagged responses) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S1-R3, S1-R4, S1-R5, S1-E5, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Note rule negatives and edge cases (off, OK/NA, spaces, changed response)
preconditions:
1. Templates with the note option on and off exist.
2. You are filling inspections against them.
steps:
1. With the option off, mark Monitor/Not OK with no note and submit.
2. Mark OK or N/A and submit.
3. Enter a note of only spaces on a flagged field.
4. Write a note then change the response to OK.
expected:
1. Option off: a Monitor or Not OK response with no note submits successfully.
2. OK or N/A: no note is required.
3. A note containing only spaces counts as empty.
4. If the technician writes a note then changes the response to OK, the note is kept.
5. Templates created before this release are unaffected until an author opens one and turns the option on; turning it on mid-inspection keeps the rule that inspection started with.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9099 (S1, Require a note on flagged responses) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S1-N1, S1-N2, S1-E1, S1-E2, S1-E3, S1-E4, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Photo-required: interaction with unconditional rule; negatives and edges
preconditions:
1. Templates exist with 'Photo required if Not OK' on, both alone and together with the unconditional 'Photo required'.
2. Photo upload can be made unavailable.
steps:
1. Mark OK/Monitor/N/A and submit.
2. With both photo rules on, read the builder summary sentence.
3. Attach a photo, satisfy the rule, then remove it and try to submit.
4. Attach a photo then change the response to OK.
5. Make photo upload unavailable and observe.
expected:
1. Option off: a Not OK response with no photo submits successfully. OK, Monitor and N/A never require a photo (Monitor requires a note, not a photograph).
2. When both 'Photo required' and 'Photo required if Not OK' are on, the unconditional rule is the one enforced and the builder summary sentence says so.
3. If the technician satisfies the rule then removes the photo, the field blocks submit again.
4. A photo attached then response changed to OK is kept.
5. If photo upload is unavailable, the technician is told why rather than being blocked by a requirement with no visible cause.
6. Templates created before this release are unaffected until an author turns the option on.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9440 (S17, Require a photo on a Not OK response) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S17-R7, S17-N1, S17-N2, S17-N3, S17-E1..E4, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Per axle is its own field type, prefilled with four measurement rows
preconditions:
1. You are signed in with Settings — Service.
2. You are editing a template.
steps:
1. Open the field-type list.
2. Add a Per axle field and read its default name, rows, units and tire/brake scope.
3. Check the Measurement field's options.
expected:
1. Per axle is its own field type offered alongside Checkbox, Text, Measurement, Photo and Instructions; the Measurement field no longer carries an axle option.
2. A new per-axle field is named "New axle set" and prefilled with four rows: tire pressure, tread depth, brake lining, push-rod travel.
3. Each row carries an author-set default unit (PSI for tire pressure; inches for tread depth, brake lining, push-rod travel) — a default the technician starts from, not a fixed value.
4. Each row states whether it is measured on the tire or on the brake: tire pressure and tread depth default to per tire, brake lining and push-rod travel to per brake.
5. A per-tire row follows the axle's Single/Dual setting at fill time; a per-brake row is always one value per side. The author does not choose how many values a side needs.
6. The template does not hold a number of axles — the technician adds them while filling.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9106 (S8, Record measurements per axle) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S8-R1..R5, S8-R9, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Filling an axle: Single/Dual, Drum/Disc, per-position values and verdicts
preconditions:
1. You are filling an inspection with a per-axle field (Work Order Lines — Create & Edit.).
2. An axle is present.
steps:
1. Set the axle to Single or Dual, and to Drum or Disc (or leave Drum/Disc blank).
2. Enter values on a per-tire row on a Dual axle, then a Single axle, and on a per-brake row.
3. Set a verdict on each value from the field menu.
expected:
1. Each axle is set to Single or Dual and to Drum or Disc; Drum or Disc may be left blank when the axle has no brakes.
2. A per-tire row on a Dual axle records four values (left outer, left inner, right inner, right outer); on a Single axle it records two; a per-brake row always records two.
3. Every value carries its own verdict — OK, Monitor, Not OK or N/A — chosen from a menu on the field.
4. The value input is tinted by its verdict and stays neutral while nothing is entered.
5. Values accept numbers and characters, including the text N/A; nothing is required and an empty value stays empty (never converted to N/A).

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9106 (S8, Record measurements per axle) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S8-R10..R13, S8-R15, S8-R16, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Derived verdicts worst-first; fill-time unit change; Single/Dual preserves
preconditions:
1. You are filling an inspection with a per-axle field.
2. An axle has several rows with mixed verdicts.
steps:
1. Set positions to a mix of OK/Monitor/Not OK and read the row and axle verdicts.
2. Change a row's unit while filling and check which positions it affects and whether readings convert.
3. Switch an axle Dual->Single->Dual and check preserved values.
expected:
1. A row's verdict is derived from its positions and an axle's from all its positions; worst wins (Not OK over Monitor over OK); neither is chosen directly.
2. Changing a row's unit while filling applies to that row across the whole axle (every position read in one unit) and does not touch other rows or axles.
3. Changing a row's unit does NOT convert readings already entered.
4. Switching an axle between Single and Dual preserves what was entered with no warning: Single keeps the outer readings as left/right, switching back restores the inner readings; preserved values live for the session only.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9106 (S8, Record measurements per axle) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S8-R14, S8-R27, S8-R17, S8-E7, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Axle diagram, add/clear/delete axles, expand behaviour
preconditions: 1. You are filling an inspection with a per-axle field on a multi-axle truck.
steps:
1. Look at the truck diagram and how tires are tinted.
2. Select a tire in the diagram.
3. Use the first axle's clear action; delete a later axle; check renumbering.
4. Expand axles one at a time and all at once.
expected:
1. A diagram of the truck shows every axle and tints each tire by the worst verdict of the rows measuring it; a tire stays grey until one of its rows has a verdict.
2. Selecting a tire in the diagram moves to that axle, row and tire.
3. The first axle can never be deleted; it carries a clear action that empties its readings and verdicts and leaves the axle in place.
4. Any axle after the first can be deleted; axles below it move up and the numbering follows.
5. Axles can be expanded one at a time or all at once; opening one does not collapse another.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9106 (S8, Record measurements per axle) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S8-R18..R22, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Per-axle negatives and edges: unanswered, N/A vs value, free text, road train
preconditions: 1. You are filling/reviewing inspections with per-axle fields in varied states.
steps:
1. Submit a required per-axle field with no verdict anywhere.
2. Leave Drum/Disc blank and check the report.
3. Enter a value with no verdict.
4. Enter the text 'N/A' as a value AND set verdict N/A.
5. Fill a 7-axle road train on desktop and phone.
6. Give an axle a verdict but no measurements.
expected:
1. A per-axle field with no verdict anywhere counts as unanswered and blocks submit when the field is required.
2. If Drum or Disc is left blank, nothing about brake type appears in the report.
3. A position with a value and no verdict is not counted as a finding and does not block submit.
4. A value of text 'N/A' and a verdict of N/A are different statements and both survive to the report distinctly.
5. Free text in a value reaches the report as entered.
6. An axle with a verdict and no measurements counts as answered. A road train of seven-plus axles stays usable on the diagram and the phone layout.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9106 (S8, Record measurements per axle) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S8-N1, S8-N2, S8-N3, S8-E1..E4, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Technician opens the reference file full-page; survives republish; negatives
preconditions:
1. A template field has a reference file.
2. You are filling an inspection (Work Order Lines — Create & Edit.); 'Work Orders — View' to open the file.
steps:
1. While filling, open the attached file.
2. Republish the template, then open the attachment on an earlier published version.
3. Try to open a file belonging to another shop; try a removed attachment; try a video upload.
expected:
1. The technician sees the attached file while filling and can open it: a full-page view in the same tab, with a close action and a download action, readable without downloading.
2. After a template is republished, instructions in earlier published versions still open their attachments.
3. Video files are rejected with a reason; a file belonging to another shop cannot be opened; a removed attachment is no longer seen by the technician.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8181 and story SV-9109 (S11, Attach a reference file to a question) and the Digital Inspections V2 specification version 18, sections S11-R4, S11-R8, S11-N1, S11-N2, S11-N3, read on 21 August 2026.
